corpus.en: The kings' navigators kneel at night.
The priest did not carry the crowns.
Navigators do not carry the kings' shield at night.
The priests did not carry the navigator's shields at night.
The kings did not polish the priests' crown at night.

accepted: the king's navigators carry shields at night
at night the king's navigators carry shields
the king's navigators are carrying shields at night
at night the king's navigators are carrying shields
the king's navigators will carry shields at night
at night the king's navigators will carry shields
toEnglish.explanation: S O V order. kuǀeǂe-ga = king-DEF; ǃoǂahe-ǃoǂahe-mu-ga = PL~navigator-POSS-DEF; ǃaka-ǃaka = PL~shield; hoǃaǃe = at.night; noku-ǂa = carry-3PL.

toLang.prompt: Kings carried the priests' crowns at night.
toLang.explanation: S O V order. kuǀeǂe-kuǀeǂe = PL~king; ǃate-ǃate-ga = PL~priest-DEF; teǀa-teǀa-mu-ga = PL~crown-POSS-DEF; hoǃaǃe = at.night; noku-ki-ǂa = carry-PST-3PL.

grammar: Word order: subject, object, verb. With one participant: subject, verb.
Plural: say the noun twice (ǃate → ǃate-ǃatega).
Marks the possessed noun (“the king's horse” = king horse-POSS). The possessor itself is bare.
Definite (“the”). A noun without it means “a” (or plain plural).
Past tense. Without it the verb is present or future.
On the verb when the subject is plural.
explain.notes: Checked against 1481 alternative analyses; the sentences rule out 1473, including: -mu appears when: possessed noun & negative.
